title: 120. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Converting Metric Area Units
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Converting Square Metres to Square Centimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square metres to square centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(5\text{ m}^2\) to \(\text{cm}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}=100\text{ cm}\), squaring the conversion factor gives \(1\text{ m}^2=(100)^2\text{ cm}^2=10{,}000\text{ cm}^2\). Therefore, \(5\text{ m}^2=5\times 10{,}000\text{ cm}^2=50{,}000\text{ cm}^2\). Option A incorrectly uses the length conversion factor without squaring it.
questions.hint: Begin with the conversion between the corresponding length units.

questions.concept: Converting Square Centimetres to Square Metres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square centimetres to square metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(300\text{ cm}^2\) to \(\text{m}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}^2=10{,}000\text{ cm}^2\), divide \(300\) by \(10{,}000\): \(300\div 10{,}000=0.03\). Therefore, \(300\text{ cm}^2=0.03\text{ m}^2\). Option B incorrectly divides by \(1{,}000\) instead of \(10{,}000\).
questions.hint: An area contains two length factors.

questions.concept: Converting Square Kilometres to Square Metres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square kilometres to square metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(2.5\text{ km}^2\) to \(\text{m}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ km}=1{,}000\text{ m}\), squaring gives \(1\text{ km}^2=(1{,}000)^2\text{ m}^2=1{,}000{,}000\text{ m}^2\). Therefore, \(2.5\text{ km}^2=2.5\times 1{,}000{,}000\text{ m}^2=2{,}500{,}000\text{ m}^2\). Option A incorrectly uses \(100{,}000\) instead of \(1{,}000{,}000\).
questions.hint: Check whether the source and target are square units or hectares.

questions.concept: Converting Square Millimetres to Square Centimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square millimetres to square centimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(45{,}000\text{ mm}^2\) to \(\text{cm}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ cm}=10\text{ mm}\), squaring gives \(1\text{ cm}^2=100\text{ mm}^2\). Therefore, \(45{,}000\text{ mm}^2=45{,}000\div 100\text{ cm}^2=450\text{ cm}^2\). Option B incorrectly divides by \(10\) instead of \(100\).
questions.hint: Begin with the conversion between the corresponding length units.

questions.concept: Converting Square Metres to Square Decimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square metres to square decimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(7.2\text{ m}^2\) to \(\text{dm}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ m}=10\text{ dm}\), squaring gives \(1\text{ m}^2=100\text{ dm}^2\). Therefore, \(7.2\text{ m}^2=7.2\times 100\text{ dm}^2=720\text{ dm}^2\). Option A incorrectly multiplies by \(10\) instead of \(100\).
questions.hint: An area contains two length factors.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in hectares to square metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(0.8\text{ ha}\) to \(\text{m}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ ha}=10{,}000\text{ m}^2\), multiply \(0.8\) by \(10{,}000\): \(0.8\times 10{,}000=8{,}000\). Therefore, \(0.8\text{ ha}=8{,}000\text{ m}^2\). Option B incorrectly uses \(1{,}000\text{ m}^2\) per hectare.
questions.hint: Check whether the source and target are square units or hectares.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square metres to hectares correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(360{,}000\text{ m}^2\) to hectares.
questions.hint: Recall how many square metres make one hectare, then decide whether to multiply or divide.

questions.concept: Converting Square Centimetres to Square Metres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square centimetres to square metres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(120{,}000\text{ cm}^2\) to \(\text{m}^2\).
questions.hint: An area contains two length factors.

questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square kilometres to hectares correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(0.45\text{ km}^2\) to hectares.
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ km}^2=1{,}000{,}000\text{ m}^2\) and \(1\text{ ha}=10{,}000\text{ m}^2\), we have \(1\text{ km}^2=100\text{ ha}\). Therefore, \(0.45\text{ km}^2=0.45\times 100\text{ ha}=45\text{ ha}\). Option B incorrectly multiplies by \(1{,}000\).
questions.hint: Check whether the source and target are square units or hectares.

questions.concept: Converting Square Centimetres to Square Millimetres
questions.learningObjective: Convert an area given in square centimetres to square millimetres correctly.
questions.question: Convert \(250{,}000\text{ cm}^2\) to \(\text{mm}^2\).
questions.explanation: Since \(1\text{ cm}=10\text{ mm}\), squaring gives \(1\text{ cm}^2=100\text{ mm}^2\). Therefore, \(250{,}000\text{ cm}^2=250{,}000\times 100\text{ mm}^2=25{,}000{,}000\text{ mm}^2\). Option A incorrectly multiplies by \(10\) instead of \(100\).
questions.hint: Begin with the conversion between the corresponding length units.
